safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It states the reference project's safe-state obligation - the 100 ms FTTI, the latching, the feedback confirmation - written by this corpus. Its own limitations field says it establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees an ASIL_D system requirement stating a 100 ms safe-state obligation with feedback confirmation and latching, mapped to ISO 26262 Part 4 Clause 7 with status `mapped`, will conclude the product meets a 100 ms FTTI with a latched and confirmed safe state. The 100 ms is the fictional goal's FTTI, the requirement is fictional, and the as_is profile of this same corpus records the real configured reaction chain as LONGER than 100 ms - so the record most likely to be read as evidence of a met FTTI is the one whose as_is counterpart documents a breach of it.

derivation_basis.locator: No source of its own. The reactions it aggregates are at src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:341-475 (DIAG_Handler) for the fault request, src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:125-163 (CONT_CheckFeedback) for the confirmation and src/app/driver/sbc/fs8x_driver/sbc_fs8x.c:160-182 (FS8x_WD_Refresh) for the driver; pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437. The 100 ms and the 30 ms mechanical opening are the fictional goal's FTTI and FB2-ASM-006, not the source.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source can open a contactor and confirm the open state, so a safe-state obligation is a real subject. It supports nothing about the 100 ms, the 5 ms classification, the latching, or the ASIL - and the as_is profile is the corpus's own evidence that the real chain does not fit the interval.

It is a requirement of the fictional reference project this corpus declares. derivation_basis names what the derivation actually rests on - for most of these, specific pinned file:line ranges, and for FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000004, FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 and FB2-SYS-SYR-000005, the explicit statement that there is no such source because the subject does not exist - and states what it does not support. No other field of the record was modified.

statement: On a confirmed safe-operating-area violation the item shall open all high-voltage contactors, disable charging and log the fault within 100 ms of the condition becoming measurable, shall confirm the open state by auxiliary feedback, and shall not leave that state on the fault disappearing.
rationale: The system-level statement of the safety goal's objective. It is written at this level because the obligation spans three allocated requirements - the software state machine, the hardware driver path and the hardware feedback path - and a requirement that any one of them could claim to satisfy would let the end-to-end timing go unstated. The figure here is the safety goal's own fault-tolerant time interval; the way that interval is spent is the technical safety concept's business, not this requirement's.

acceptance_criteria.measure: Time from the condition becoming measurable to the open state being confirmed
Open states confirmed by auxiliary feedback
Faults that do not clear on the disappearance of the condition

safety_allocation.mitigation: Latched fault state, auxiliary feedback confirmation, the hardware watchdog path and the independent monitor

limitations: Synthetic. This requirement describes a hypothetical programme and establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.

System-level only. It does not carry the hardware or software detail, which lives in FB2-HW-TSR-* and FB2-SW-SWR-*. Where this record and those records disagree, neither is silently preferred and the disagreement is raised as a finding.
Not verified against the product. Every measure that touches its allocated requirements is a synthetic fixture or a blocked record; see the FB2-VER-EXE-* set.
